title: Chevron Corporation 8-K Filing — Q1 2026 Guidance
summary: Chevron Corporation provided preliminary Q1 2026 guidance on April 9, 2026, citing significant negative timing effects of $2.7–$3.7 billion from derivatives marking and LIFO accounting in a rising commodity price environment, partially offset by upstream commodity price benefits of $1.6–$2.2 billion. The company also disclosed reduced production in the Middle East (Israel and the Partitioned Zone) and downtime at Tengizchevroil, with total production expected at 3.8–3.9 million barrels of oil-equivalent per day. A litigation reserve charge of $350–$400 million is expected to affect downstream earnings.
key_points: Timing effects expected to adversely affect Q1 2026 earnings by $2.7–$3.7 billion due to derivatives marking-to-market in rising commodity price environment; majority in Downstream segment, expected to unwind in future periods
Working capital expected to result in net outflow of $2–$4 billion, reflecting normal Q1 activity and higher commodity price environment
Upstream commodity price benefits of $1.6–$2.2 billion compared to Q4 2025
Production guidance of 3.8–3.9 MMBOED reflects downtime at Tengizchevroil and reduced production in Middle East (Israel and Partitioned Zone)
Litigation reserve charge of $350–$400 million related to ceased operations; treated as special item
Weighted-average shares outstanding approximately 1.981 billion; share repurchases largely offset by employee stock option exercises generating ~$1 billion financing cash inflow
Company cites 'heightened commodity price volatility related to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East' as affecting Q1 results
why_it_matters: This 8-K filing provides early Q1 2026 earnings guidance for a major integrated energy company, offering investors insight into commodity price impacts, production disruptions from Middle East tensions, and non-recurring charges. While not a macro data release, the guidance signals how geopolitical conflict is affecting oil company operations and earnings timing. Full Q1 results expected around May 1, 2026.
macro_context: Chevron attributes commodity price volatility and Middle East production impacts to 'the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.' The filing shows how geopolitical tensions are directly affecting energy sector earnings through both price volatility (favorable for upstream) and physical production constraints (unfavorable for volume). Working capital outflows reflect higher inventory values in a rising commodity price environment.
market_structure_context: The filing is relevant to commodities (oil) and equities markets. Production guidance of 3.8-3.9 MMBOED affects oil supply expectations. The timing effects from derivatives marking in a rising price environment (negative $2.7-3.7B) versus commodity price benefits (positive $1.6-2.2B) reflects how financial hedging creates earnings volatility distinct from underlying physical performance. Working capital outflows of $2-4B indicate higher inventory values in a rising commodity price environment.
